title: Well-formed SLO monitoring — shared event-set recording rules, burn-rate alerts, routing and runbooks
code_snippet:
groups:
  # --- The event set, defined ONCE. One valid/bad pair PER WINDOW the alert uses. ---
  # valid = requests excluding health checks, /metrics and client cancellations (499)
  # bad   = server fault (5xx). 4xx is the caller's fault and stays "good".
  - name: sli_events
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      - record: sli:http_requests_valid:rate1h
        expr: sum by (job) (rate(http_requests_total{path!~"/health.*|/metrics",code!="499"}[1h]))
      - record: sli:http_requests_bad:rate1h
        expr: sum by (job) (rate(http_requests_total{path!~"/health.*|/metrics",code=~"5.."}[1h]))
      - record: sli:http_requests_valid:rate5m
        expr: sum by (job) (rate(http_requests_total{path!~"/health.*|/metrics",code!="499"}[5m]))
      - record: sli:http_requests_bad:rate5m
        expr: sum by (job) (rate(http_requests_total{path!~"/health.*|/metrics",code=~"5.."}[5m]))

  # --- SLO: 99.9% availability over 30 days ---
  # Error budget = 0.1% of VALID REQUESTS (request-based). The familiar ~43.2 min/month is
  # the time-based budget for the same target; here it is only a request-based
  # approximation under uniform traffic, so we alert on burn rate instead.
  - name: slo_burn_rate
    rules:
      - alert: SLOBurnRateCritical
        expr: |
          sli:http_requests_bad:rate1h / sli:http_requests_valid:rate1h > 14.4 * 0.001
          and
          sli:http_requests_bad:rate5m / sli:http_requests_valid:rate5m > 14.4 * 0.001
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: 'SLO burn rate 14.4x - 2% of 30-day budget spent in 1h (exhausts in ~50h if sustained)'
          runbook_url: 'https://wiki/runbooks/slo-burn-rate'
          dashboard_url: 'https://grafana/d/slo?var-service=payment'

# Routing: severity critical -> the org's page-worthy policy (primary: PagerDuty;
#          secondary: #alerts-critical via continue: true). Example mapping, not a rule.
# Dashboard: RED method with a $service variable
expected_feedback: No violations. (1) The whole snippet is a single valid Prometheus rule file -- one `groups:` mapping containing both the recording rules and the alert -- so it loads as written. (2) The event set is defined once, with a valid/bad pair per window (1h and 5m), so availability, error rate and the burn-rate alert all use the same series and remain exact complements; changing the exclusion list cannot make them drift apart. (3) valid and good are both stated: health checks, /metrics and client-cancelled (499) requests are excluded from valid, 4xx stays good, bad = 5xx. (4) The error budget is declared as 0.1% of valid requests -- request-based -- and the ~43.2 min figure is marked as a request-based approximation under uniform traffic rather than presented as a downtime guarantee. (5) The alert is genuinely multi-window: the 1h long window decides whether to alert and the 5m short window gates 'still burning now'. Using the same window on both sides would look like a multi-window rule and behave like a single-window one. (6) severity maps to the org's page-worthy routing policy, which may have a primary action receiver plus secondary visibility receivers. (7) runbook_url and dashboard_url both present. (8) RED-method dashboard with variable templating. Burn-rate arithmetic checks out: 14.4 x (1h / 720h) = 2% of budget per hour, and 720h / 14.4 = ~50h to exhaust if sustained -- a summary claiming 14.4x 'exhausts the 30-day budget in 2 hours' would be wrong by more than an order of magnitude.
